newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuba, Dominican Republic establish consular ties.
newsitem.headline: Cuba, Dominican Republic establish consular ties.

text.p: Cuba and the Dominican Republic agreed on Friday to establish consular ties, partially renewing diplomatic links broken more than three decades ago.
The agreement was signed at the foreign ministry in Havana by visiting deputy foreign minister Minou Tavarez and Cuban deputy foreign minister Maria de los Angeles Flores.
They also signed an understanding on migration issues under which both countries will undertake to repatriate any nationals of the other country arriving illegally in their territory.
Tavarez, who arrived in Havana on Thursday and is in Cuba until Sunday, told reporters it was not yet known exactly when consular offices would be opened in Havana and Santo Domingo.
While the two countries have not had formal relations, in recent years they have had increasing business, travel and sports ties.
A Cuban deputy foreign minister, Jorge Bolanos, travelled to the Dominican Republic last August to attend the swearing in of President Leonel Fernandez.

Foreign Minister Roberto Robaina went to Santo Domingo earlier this month as part of a trip to Central America and the Caribbean with a message from President Fidel Castro condemning U.S. Congress moves to tighten the 35-year-old U.S. economic embargo on Havana.
Tavarez travelled to Cuba last November, bringing with her a cargo of aid for Cuba after Hurricane Lili swept the island in October, causing damage to homes and crops.
The Dominican Republic broke off relations with Cuba 33 years ago, soon after the 1959 revolution that brought Castro to power.
Fernandez's election ended decades of almost uninterrupted political dominance by the rightist dictator Rafael Trujillo and his one-time protege Joaquin Balaguer.
